Prior PET/CT showed postoperative changes after pancreatic-tail and splenic resection without abnormal hypermetabolic foci in the operative bed; para-aortic nodes and small pulmonary nodules were not hypermetabolic, with regular follow-up recommended, while some mildly avid findings were favored to be inflammatory or postoperative changes.
The ECG during the second hospitalization was normal, with no documented electrocardiographic abnormality.
The ECG was normal and resting echocardiography showed no obvious abnormality during the third hospitalization.
The ECG during the fourth hospitalization was normal.
The first hospitalization showed mild macrocytic-anemia-related abnormalities, mildly elevated CA19-9 at 40.7 U/mL, and other nonspecific abnormalities.

The second hospitalization showed persistent macrocytic-anemia-related abnormalities, hemoglobin 128 g/L with reduced red-cell count, CA19-9 increased to 60.9 U/mL, and low prealbumin with coagulation-related abnormalities.
The third hospitalization continued to show macrocytic-anemia-related abnormalities, with CA19-9 rising further to 105.7 U/mL, low fibrinogen, prolonged thrombin time, and elevated cystatin C.

During the fourth hospitalization, CA19-9 was markedly elevated to 361.2 U/mL, with elevated CA242, CA72-4, and alkaline phosphatase, leukocytosis and neutrophilia, persistent macrocytic red-cell indices, and elevated cystatin C. This marker trend requires further oncologic assessment, but progression cannot be diagnosed from markers alone.
Intravenous administration of chemotherapeutic drugs was performed during the first hospitalization.
Intravenous administration of chemotherapeutic drugs was performed during the second hospitalization.
Intravenous administration of chemotherapeutic drugs was performed during the third hospitalization.
The fourth hospitalization documented intravenous administration of chemotherapeutic drugs, confirming that the current maintenance chemotherapy was administered.
